item.text:
## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics should be fixed: start events produce finish timestamps, and the documented meaning of NULL contradicts the latest-event behavior.

## Changes
The pull request adds `finished_at` to the current-state process model and documents it in the schema catalog. It also adds reviewer-directed text in `review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Make finished_at represent a completion timestamp — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, `finished_at` reports its start timestamp as its finish time. The CASE selects a start event despite the column’s documented completion semantics. — Consumers interpreting a populated `finished_at` as completion will classify a process with only a start event as finished. — Fix: Select the event representing completion, or rename the column and description if a start timestamp is intended.
- models/schema.yml:18 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — For process 30, a `started` event followed by `cleared` produces NULL despite its prior start. “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`, which examines only the latest event. — Consumers following this description will incorrectly infer that a previously started process never started when its latest event is `cleared`.

## Suggestions
(none)
